$description: ui-interaction-dev's words: one meaning each. A spec rule and the guides use these terms in these senses only.

concepts.definition: An element a pointer press can turn into a drag.
avoid: drag source, when the item is the thing moved

concepts.definition: An element that accepts a dragged item: a list, a lane, a well, or an item for a combine.
avoid: droppable, as a noun for an item

concepts.definition: The test a press must pass before it becomes a drag: a distance for mouse and pen, a delay with a tolerance for touch.
A press on a draggable that has not yet met its activation constraint; nothing on screen has changed.
A drag past its activation constraint: the pointer is captured and the item follows it.
The paint of an item being carried: raised, offset up, following the pointer. Not a box change.
avoid: grabbed, which echoes the deprecated aria-grabbed

concepts.definition: The 2px line, with a terminal ring, that marks where a dragged item will land.
The hover tint over a container that would take the dragged item, when it is not the item's own.
A way to reach every drag outcome with taps or clicks and no path (WCAG 2.5.7), such as the Move menu.
avoid: keyboard alternative, which is a separate requirement

concepts.definition: The control on an item, named Move <item>, that opens the menu of where it can go.
The region that takes the pointer for a part: its box, or a transparent ::before around a smaller part.
avoid: target size, when the painted box is meant

concepts.definition: A part's paint (fill, gradient, text colour) as distinct from its box; hover changes the face only.
The same check run against the code without the change, which must fail.
Of a spec rule: an implementation's test proved it, with a negative control, and the record says where and how.
Of a spec rule: a primary source states it; no test here has proved it yet.
Of a spec rule: primary sources disagree; both positions are recorded and the rule says what is safe either way.
